```{r}
source("whitening.R")
source("autocov.R")

```

# Part A
Test the whitening function:

```{r}
set.seed(123)

# Generate a multivariate time series-like dataset
n <- 1000
p <- 3

# Create correlated variables with different scales
A <- matrix(c(
  2.0,  0.8,  0.3,
  0.5,  1.5,  0.7,
  0.2, -0.4,  1.0
), nrow = p, byrow = TRUE)

E <- matrix(rnorm(n * p), nrow = n, ncol = p)
X <- E %*% t(A)

# Add a nonzero mean to each variable
X <- sweep(X, 2, c(5, -3, 10), "+")

# Check the original covariance
cat("Covariance before whitening:\n")
print(round(cov(X), 3))

# Apply the whitening function
Z <- whiten_data(X)

cat("\nCovariance after whitening:\n")
print(round(cov(Z), 6))

cat("\nMeans after whitening:\n")
print(round(colMeans(Z), 10))
```

Test the function that returns the autocovariance matrices for a set of lags:

```{r}
lags <- 1:5

# Use the same standardized test set as above
Sigma_lags <- autocov_matrices(Z, lags = lags)
Sigma_lags
```


# Part C

I tried to draft a function for the ladle quantities, but in the end I just calculated f_0 without a function. I tried to do it so that it would be easy to convert it into a function later on though. It's not very good yet :D

```{r}
data = Z
tau = 1
n_boot = 200
bootstrap_method = block_bootstrap
diagonalizer = AMUSE_diagonalizer


# we first calculate B_hat 
# so the first k columns of the diagonalizer computed from the original sample
B_hat <- diagonalizer(data, tau)$u_tau

# then we calculate B_star 
# B_star is an array
B_star_array <- replicate(n_boot, {
  X_j <- bootstrap_method(data = data, B = 10)
  B_hat <- diagonalizer(data = X_j)$u_tau
})

f_k(B_hat, B_star_array, 3)

```


# Part D Simulation Study 
Now we use the simulation setting specified as Setting 1 in the paper to investigate the behaviour of our implementation.

First we test the methods once and plot the results of f, phi and g to verify the results are as expected. We use the stationary bootstrap method, expected block size of 20 and the SOBI estimator here. 

```{r}
X <- generate_ladle_data(n = 2000)
Z <- whiten_data(X)


data = Z
tau = 1:12
n_boot = 200
bootstrap_method = stationary_bootstrap
diagonalizer = SOBI_diagonalizer


# we first calculate B_hat 
# so the first k columns of the diagonalizer computed from the original sample
res <- diagonalizer(data, tau)

B_hat <- res$u_tau
Lambda <- res$lambda

# then we calculate B_star 
# B_star is an array
B_star_array <- replicate(n_boot, {
  X_j <- bootstrap_method(data = data, B = 20)
  B_hat <- diagonalizer(data = X_j, lags = tau)$u_tau
})



res <- diagonalizer_full(data = Z, 
                         lags = 1:12, 
                         n_boot = 200, 
                         bootstrap_method = stationary_bootstrap, 
                         block_size = 20, 
                         diagonalizer = SOBI_diagonalizer)

B_hat <- res$B_hat
B_star <- res$B_star
lambda <- res$lambda

f_s <- sapply(1:9, function(k){f_k(B_hat, B_star, k)})
phi_s <- sapply(1:9, function(k){phi(lambda, k)})
g_s <- f_s + phi_s

```
```{r}
plot(f_s, type = "b", xlab = "component", ylab = "criterion", col = "black", ylim = c(0, 0.6))
lines(phi_s, type = "b", col = "red")
lines(g_s, type = "b", col = "green")
legend(x = "topright", legend = c("f", "phi", "g"),  lty = c(1), col = c("black", "red", "green"))

```

Next we repeat the bootstrapping and estimation 2000 times to gauge the error. I'm not re-doing the simulation now, but that might also be needed. 

```{r}
# we repeat the calculation 2000 times
set.seed(20261024)
signal_dim_estimates <- replicate(200, {
  res <- diagonalizer_full(data = Z, 
                         lags = 2, 
                         n_boot = 200, 
                         bootstrap_method = block_bootstrap, 
                         block_size = 20, 
                         diagonalizer = AMUSE_diagonalizer)
  g_s <- sapply(1:9, function(k){g_k(res$lambda, res$B_hat, res$B_star, k)})
  which.min(g_s)
})

signal_dim_estimates
summary(signal_dim_estimates)

```
